title: Create, complete or edit logic diagrams and truth tables
footer: 2.4 Lesson 3: Create, complete or edit logic diagrams and truth tables
starter: A security light should come on when it is dark AND movement is detected, unless the test switch is on. Write that rule in your own words, then underline the logic words.
starterAnswer: Accept any sensible attempt: this is a hook, not an assessment.
Look for the vocabulary from the lesson objectives appearing in students' own words.
Students who are stuck should still write something: the experience will correct it.
starterNote: Take two or three answers, then leave it open. Come back to it in the plenary, when they can answer it properly.

stations.name: From words to logic
facts: Find the inputs and the output in the scenario.
Decide which parts go in brackets, then build from the inputs to the output.
stations.challenge: How do you create a logic diagram from a scenario?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Find the inputs and the output in the scenario.
Also credit: Look for the words 'and', 'or', 'not', 'either' and 'regardless'.

questions.q: 'The alarm sounds if the door is open AND it is night.' Which gate is needed?
'Regardless of the sensors, the alarm always sounds if the manual button is pressed.' How is the button joined to the rest?

stations.name: Scenario 1: the shop alarm
facts: A shop alarm sounds (X) if the door sensor is triggered (A) AND the shop is closed (B).
Whatever the sensors say, it always sounds if the panic button is pressed (C).
stations.challenge: Build the shop alarm circuit, then complete its truth table.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: A shop alarm sounds (X) if the door sensor is triggered (A) AND the shop is closed (B).
Also credit: Whatever the sensors say, it always sounds if the panic button is pressed (C).

questions.q: Build the shop alarm circuit: X = (A AND B) OR C.
questions.a: Any circuit equivalent to (A AND B) OR C (the site accepts any layout that gives the same truth table)

questions.q: Complete the truth table for the shop alarm.
questions.a: Truth table for X = (A AND B) OR C over 3 inputs (8 rows); output is 1 wherever the expression is true

stations.name: Scenario 2: the hospital lift
facts: A hospital lift has two doors (A and B). An alarm sounds (X)...
if either door is still open,
AND either the lift is moving (C) OR it is overloaded (D).
stations.challenge: Why do both halves of this circuit use OR gates?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: A hospital lift has two doors (A and B). An alarm sounds (X)...
Also credit: if either door is still open,

questions.q: Build the hospital lift circuit: X = (A OR B) AND (C OR D).
questions.a: Any circuit equivalent to (A OR B) AND (C OR D) (the site accepts any layout that gives the same truth table)

questions.q: In the hospital lift, when does the alarm sound?
questions.a: When at least one door is open, and the lift is either moving or overloaded

stations.name: Scenario 3: the greenhouse
facts: A greenhouse heater runs (X) if the gardener switches it on (A) OR the timer starts it (B).
When a window is opened it sends 1, and the heater must switch off.
stations.challenge: Why does the window sensor need a NOT gate?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: A greenhouse heater runs (X) if the gardener switches it on (A) OR the timer starts it (B).
Also credit: A window sensor (C) normally sends 0.

questions.q: Build the greenhouse circuit: X = (A OR B) AND NOT C.
questions.a: Any circuit equivalent to (A OR B) AND NOT C (the site accepts any layout that gives the same truth table)

questions.q: Complete the truth table for the greenhouse.
questions.a: Truth table for X = (A OR B) AND NOT C over 3 inputs (8 rows); output is 1 wherever the expression is true

stations.name: Editing a diagram
facts: Sometimes a diagram needs changing to match a new rule.
Check each gate against the scenario, one at a time.
Test your change with a truth table.
stations.challenge: The shop alarm should now need the panic button AND the shop to be closed. How would the circuit change?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Sometimes a diagram needs changing to match a new rule.
Also credit: Check each gate against the scenario, one at a time.

questions.q: A circuit should output 1 only when both sensors are on, but it uses an OR gate. How do you fix it?
questions.a: Replace the OR gate with an AND gate

questions.q: The greenhouse window sensor is wired straight into the AND gate, without a NOT gate. What goes wrong?
questions.a: The heater runs only when a window is open

stations.name: Reading diagrams
facts: To write an expression from a diagram, start at the output and work backwards.
Each gate becomes an operator, and each gate feeding another becomes brackets.
stations.challenge: Write the expression for the diagram in the experience.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: To write an expression from a diagram, start at the output and work backwards.
Also credit: Each gate becomes an operator, and each gate feeding another becomes brackets.

questions.q: Write the Boolean expression for this logic diagram.
questions.a: Q = NOT A AND (B OR C) (or any equivalent expression)

questions.q: Write the Boolean expression for this logic diagram.
questions.a: X = (A OR B) AND NOT C (or any equivalent expression)

final.name: Final challenge: design and test

questions.q: Build the security light: Q = (A AND B) AND NOT C.
questions.a: Any circuit equivalent to (A AND B) AND NOT C (the site accepts any layout that gives the same truth table)

questions.q: Complete the truth table for NOT (A AND B) OR C.
questions.a: Truth table for Q = NOT (A AND B) OR C over 3 inputs (8 rows); output is 1 wherever the expression is true

final.note: Students should have predicted these on the worksheet before tapping the star. Mark the prediction, not just the final answer.

exam.q: A fire door alarm sounds (Q) when the door is open (D) AND the building is locked (L), or when the test button (T) is pressed. Write the Boolean expression.
points: Whatever the sensors say, it always sounds if the panic button is pressed (C).
A shop alarm sounds (X) if the door sensor is triggered (A) AND the shop is closed (B).
A hospital lift has two doors (A and B). An alarm sounds (X)...
Accept any other correct point relevant to the question.
exam.note: One mark per point, to a maximum of 2.

exam.q: Draw the logic diagram for your expression.
points: To write an expression from a diagram, start at the output and work backwards.
Sometimes a diagram needs changing to match a new rule.
Accept any other correct point relevant to the question.
exam.note: One mark per point, to a maximum of 3.

common: Naming a term without saying what it does: most questions need the term and its purpose.
Answering 'it's faster' or 'it's better' with no reason: link it to the characteristic the question is about.
Repeating the question in the answer and stopping there.
